small_guidance:
- The 7-deep nested Python loop (PD·PH·PW·MK³·KD·KH·KW = ~13K iterations per program) is the bottleneck; collapse the maxpool window into the same accumulator and tile the output spatial axis so a single program produces a vector of pooled outputs via tl.arange, not scalar loops.
- Use channels_last-style blocking on OC instead of one program per (N, OC); a BLOCK_OC of 16 lets the inner reduction reuse loaded x_vals across all output channels and turns the IC×OC contraction into a tl.dot.
- Add an autotune sweep over (BLOCK_OC=8/16, BLOCK_SPATIAL=8/16/32, num_warps=4/8, num_stages=2/3) — current num_warps=2 with no tiling leaves the SM grossly underutilized (only 128*16=2048 programs, each doing scalar work).
large_guidance:
- Redesign as scatter-add: one program per (N, IC-tile, input-spatial-tile) reads x once, computes the input×weight outer product over OC and the KD·KH·KW kernel taps, and atomically scatters into a small intermediate ConvT output buffer (or, better, directly into a per-(N,OC) maxpool/sum reduction buffer using atomic_max + atomic_add). This matches the ConvTranspose3d skill (scatter-add of input×kernel outer product) instead of the current gather-with-divisibility-check, which wastes ~7/8 of iterations on invalid stride positions.
- Alternative two-kernel pipeline: kernel A does ConvTranspose3d with channels_last via im2col-style GEMM (program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), tl.dot over IC·KD·KH·KW); kernel B fuses maxpool3d→GAP→clamp as a single reduction over the OD·OH·OW axis per (N,OC). This separates the heavy compute from the trivial reduction and lets each be tuned independently.
- Fold scale into weight at init (already done) and additionally precompute the valid (kd,kh,kw)→input-offset table per output position at host time; pass as a constexpr-shaped tensor so the kernel inner loop becomes a dense GEMM rather than masked scalar work.
